decisions.mark: names MBEDTLS_THREADING_C and MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD as the gating macros
decisions.detail: QUOTE: `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is commented out in `include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h:3787`, and `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` is commented out at `:2196`. So `threading.c` compiles to nothing useful, and every lock site in the library sits behind `#if defined(MBEDTLS_THREADING_C)`. | WHY: The answer names both MBEDTLS_THREADING_C and MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD and says lock sites are gated behind MBEDTLS_THREADING_C.

decisions.mark: states that the shipped mbedtls_config.h leaves BOTH threading macros undefined, so a default build defines neither
decisions.detail: QUOTE: `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is commented out in `include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h:3787`, and `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` is commented out at `:2196`. | WHY: The answer states that the shipped config leaves both threading macros commented out (undefined), so the default build defines neither.

decisions.mark: concludes that a default build of mbedtls creates no threads at all, and that the pthread example compiles to a stub main under that condition
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "Library threads:** none. The index found four spawn sites, all in `programs/`" and "`MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is commented out ... So `threading.c` compiles to nothing useful" | WHY: The answer says the library creates no threads by default, but it never says the pthread example compiles to a stub main under a default build. It lists `ssl_pthread_server.c:277` as a spawn site instead.

decisions.mark: states BOTH halves of the contrast: that nothing in library/ creates a thread, AND that library/ nonetheless supplies the mutex abstraction used by threaded callers
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "**Library threads:** none. The index found four spawn sites, all in `programs/`... `library/` has none." and "The mutex type is `mbedtls_threading_mutex_t`. Lock and unlock go through function-pointer variables (`threading.c:103`) that default to pthread implementations, and `MBEDTLS_THREADING_ALT` lets you substitute your own." | WHY: The answer states that library/ spawns no threads and that the library supplies the mutex abstraction (`mbedtls_threading_mutex_t`, pluggable lock functions) used when threading is enabled.
